modules.title: Phonon mode classification and frozen phonons
modules.summary: Identify the entire degenerate subspace at Γ, then freeze a selected vibration into an exportable structure.

modules.title: Band compatibility relations and connectivity

lessons.title: How should degenerate vibrations be classified?
lessons.summary: Symmetry acts on a mode subspace; an arbitrarily selected individual eigenvector may not be invariant.

sections.title: Start with mass-weighted coordinates
sections.text: Phonopy diagonalizes the mass-weighted dynamical matrix. Its eigenvectors e_j differ from physical atomic displacements u_j by a square root of mass. Rotating atomic displacements requires both Cartesian-vector rotation and permutation of equivalent atoms.

sections.title: A degenerate subspace has no unique basis
sections.text: Orthonormal eigenvectors of the same frequency may be mixed unitarily. Assigning an irreducible label to each column separately can produce contradictory labels after changing eigenvectors. First collect the complete degenerate space E, then test whether every group operation preserves it.

sections.title: Check characters and closure together
sections.text: character  is invariant under internal  change of basis . Beyond character inner products, check that D(g)E lies within E and that columns are orthogonal. A frequency tolerance that is too small splits degeneracies; one that is too large may merge distinct physical branches. A merged subspace may contain several irreducible components.

sections.title: Classification scope of the first release
sections.text: At Γ, lattice translations carry no Bloch phase. This site initially supports explicitly covered point-group character tables and complete available subspaces. Other point groups or nonclosed spaces display characters and the reason while remaining unclassified. A label describes spatial symmetry; it does not alone give Raman intensity.

lessons.title: Freeze a vibrational mode into a structure
lessons.summary: Separate mode direction from displacement amplitude to generate POSCAR / CIF structures for further calculations.

sections.title: A frozen structure is a mode snapshot
sections.text: Specify the mode, real-space phase, and displacement amplitude, then add displacements to equilibrium atomic positions. Normalization uses the maximum envelope of mass-unweighted complex displacements; the actual maximum displacement at the chosen phase may be smaller than A. This amplitude is a user-specified geometric scale, not a finite-temperature root-mean-square displacement or evidence of an energy minimum.

sections.title: The supercell must accommodate the wavelength
sections.text: Periodic boundaries in a diagonal supercell [n1,n2,n3] require each ni qi to be an integer. Γ needs only one primitive cell; q=(1/2,0,0) requires an even period in the first direction. Simply duplicating a primitive-cell image does not automatically meet this condition.

sections.title: Export and subsequent verification
sections.text: Exports retain elements, lattice vectors and displaced coordinates. POSCAR groups atoms by element, and the complete result includes the atom-order mapping; CIF preserves the frozen-atom list order. CIF writes all atoms in P1 to avoid retaining parent operations without reidentification. Send the result to structure standardization or an external electronic-structure program for energy and force calculations.

sections.title: Positive and negative amplitudes and the origin convention
sections.text: A mode's overall complex phase can change the snapshot direction, and different combinations within a degenerate subspace may generate different distortions. Retain the original file, q, mode index, phase,  supercell , and amplitude to reconstruct the same snapshot.

lessons.title: How can imported modes be validated?
lessons.summary: Confirm the primitive cell, atom order, and eigenvectors before discussing mode labels.

sections.title: Structures and eigenvectors must correspond atom by atom
sections.text: The frequency file and supplementary structure must use the same primitive cell and atom order. Identical chemical formulas do not establish atom correspondence. Missing masses, coordinate units or eigenvectors require additional data; an arbitrary structure must not be inferred from the material name.

sections.title: Acoustic zero modes provide an independent check
sections.text: A Γ-point rigid translation gives identical actual displacements for every atom, while  mass weighting  eigenvector amplitudes should scale as √m. After reconstruction using e/√m, all atoms must move in the same direction with equal amplitudes.

sections.title: Distinguish numerical error from physical symmetry breaking
sections.text: If nominally degenerate frequencies split slightly, first check numerical tolerances and structural precision. The complete identified structural symmetry specifies geometric relations only. Subspace closure can fail if the input dynamical matrix or modes do not respect those symmetries.

sections.title: Save evidence, not merely labels
sections.text: Record characters, decomposition multiplicities, closure residuals, input files and calculation version together. Frequencies and eigenvectors of the built-in diatomic models are teaching constructions suitable for checking analytic results, not first-principles spectra of real materials.

lessons.title: How do representations at high-symmetry points branch along a line?
lessons.summary: Restrict endpoint representations to the path's  little group  to obtain compatibility relations.

sections.title: Symmetry is usually reduced along a path
sections.text: The Γ point of a two-dimensional square lattice can have C4v symmetry, while a generic point on Γ–X retains only the mirror containing that line. Restricting the endpoint's two-dimensional E representation to this Cs subgroup gives one mirror-even and one mirror-odd one-dimensional branch.

sections.title: Restriction is not guessing a new table
sections.text: Retain only subgroup operations, evaluate the original representation's characters on them, and take inner products with subgroup irreducible characters. For Cs, the operations are E and mirror m, and the restricted E representation has characters (2,0).

sections.title: Dimension conservation is a necessary check
sections.text: The sum of branch dimensions times  multiplicity  must equal the endpoint  representation dimension . Compatibility relations constrain allowed connectivity, but do not determine every branch energy, bandwidth, or actual band order in all materials.

sections.title: How the models relate to real bands
sections.text: The demonstration uses an explicitly specified two-orbital, two-dimensional periodic Hamiltonian with parameters in model energy units. It gives a testable example of representation restriction and protected crossings; it is not presented as the electronic structure of Si or GaAs.

lessons.title: Why do some crossings survive while others gap out?
lessons.summary: Use mirror eigenvalues to assess mixing, then test with a symmetry-breaking term.

sections.title: Terms preserving the mirror cannot mix different mirror labels
sections.text: On a mirror-symmetric path, take two states with mirror eigenvalues +1 and −1. If the Hamiltonian commutes with the mirror, their matrix element equals its negative and must vanish.

sections.title: An allowed crossing need not actually occur
sections.text: Symmetry forbids hybridization, but whether the two energies meet still depends on model parameters. The demonstration model has a visible crossing; changing the band-order parameter can shift the crossing or move it off the path.

sections.title: Add a symmetry-breaking term and diagonalize directly
sections.text: Near a crossing write H=εI+d_zσ_z+δσ_x. δ mixes the two mirror labels and breaks the corresponding mirror symmetry. At the original crossing d_z=0, the two eigenvalues differ by 2|δ|. The parent compatibility table is then a reference rather than a strict label for the actual states.

sections.title: Trace results back to their assumptions
sections.text: Check the returned covariance residual and actual retained symmetries before interpreting crossings. This demonstration does not perform general material topology classification; existing tight-binding and Wilson-loop tools can further investigate suitable models.

lessons.title: SOC, double-valued mirror representations and Kramers degeneracy
lessons.summary: Use the Rashba model to distinguish splitting at generic k from degeneracy at time-reversal-invariant momenta.

sections.title: A spinful mirror differs from an ordinary mirror
sections.text: The spin-1/2 lift of a mirror squares to −1, so its eigenvalues are +i and −i. These are one-dimensional mirror branches of the double group and cannot be directly identified with the ±1 labels of ordinary Cs.

sections.title: Time reversal connects k and −k
sections.text: With T preserved and T²=−1, the Kramers theorem requires double degeneracy at  time reversal -invariant  wavevector . At a generic k, the partner lies at −k; a system lacking inversion can therefore have spin splitting at generic k.

sections.title: A periodic Rashba model
sections.text: Take H=ε(k)I+α(sin ky σx−sin kx σy). At Γ and X the sine terms vanish; generic points on Γ–X can be split. Adding Bzσz breaks time reversal, so endpoint degeneracy can no longer be claimed as guaranteed by Kramers' theorem.

sections.title: Compare symbolic checks with the plot
sections.text: Set SOC and Zeeman parameters independently to zero or nonzero values and inspect endpoints, generic points and mirror labels. Guided exercises first ask which symmetries survive and then explain the changes in the curves.

lessons.title: How does a set of vibrations determine free energy and heat capacity?
lessons.summary: Sum from one quantum harmonic oscillator to the entire  primitive cell , keeping zero-point energy and statistical weights explicit.

sections.title: Zero-point energy persists at zero temperature
sections.text: For a positive-frequency mode, the energy quantum is hν. Its zero-point energy is hν/2; Bose occupation gives additional thermal excitation. Here ν is ordinary frequency, not angular frequency, so no extra factor of 2π should be included.

sections.title: Obtain F, S, and Cv from the partition function
sections.text: Free energy includes zero-point and thermal-occupation terms, and entropy follows from (U−F)/T. Constant-volume heat capacity measures the temperature dependence of internal energy. Stable numerical implementations must handle T=0 and both very small and very large x correctly.

sections.title: Per primitive cell and per mole of primitive cells
sections.text: A  primitive cell  containing n atoms has 3n  phonon  branches. The site displays energies in kJ/mol  primitive cell  and entropy and heat capacity in J/(mol  primitive cell  K), retaining conversion per  primitive cell . Per-mole  primitive cell  and per-mole-atom quantities differ by a factor n.

sections.title: Scope of the harmonic approximation
sections.text: This is harmonic phonon thermodynamics at fixed structure. It excludes electronic, magnetic, and defect free energies and does not automatically yield constant-pressure heat capacity, thermal expansion, or lattice thermal conductivity. Phonon data at several volumes can support a subsequent quasiharmonic extension.

lessons.title: Which  phonon  data can determine bulk heat capacity?
lessons.summary: High-symmetry paths, complete meshes and DOS answer different questions.

sections.title: A path is not a Brillouin-zone integral
sections.text: band.yaml normally samples only one or several high-symmetry lines. Directly averaging these frequencies overweights those lines and cannot represent the whole  Brillouin zone . Use a properly weighted mesh or a clearly normalized total DOS covering all branches.

sections.title: Check weights before summing modes
sections.text: Irreducible-mesh q points carry weights equal to the number of equivalent points they represent. After normalization, all q-point weights sum to 1, and all 3n branches at each point must be included. The DOS must integrate to 3n modes per primitive cell; a partial atomic projected DOS cannot replace the total DOS.

sections.title: Handle imaginary and zero frequencies explicitly
sections.text: Negative signed frequencies usually encode imaginary frequencies, where stable-harmonic-oscillator thermodynamics does not apply; they must not be silently discarded. Exact zeros in a discrete mesh also require an explicit policy. If excluded, the lost mode weight must be reported and the result must not be described as a complete harmonic model.

sections.title: An existing thermal_properties.yaml
sections.text: You can directly read a temperature table already calculated by Phonopy and plot it after checking energy and heat-capacity units. Import retains the file's input computational cell; it cannot automatically be relabeled per  primitive cell . Internal energy may be derived from available F, S, T using U=F+TS and labeled accordingly. Missing zero-point energy remains unknown.

lessons.title: What can Einstein and Debye models explain?
lessons.summary: Check the model using its low- and high-temperature limits, then explain differences at intermediate temperatures.

sections.title: Einstein: place all vibrations at one frequency
sections.text: The Einstein model places all 3n modes at the frequency associated with characteristic temperature θE. Thermal excitation is exponentially suppressed at low temperature; increasing θE shifts the rise in heat capacity to higher temperatures.

sections.title: Debye: retain the three-dimensional low-frequency continuum
sections.text: The Debye model uses a DOS proportional to squared frequency below a cutoff and normalizes the total mode count to 3n. It gives low-temperature T³ heat capacity. This is a result for a three-dimensional acoustic continuum, not a universal rule for all dimensions or excitations.

sections.title: The same high-temperature mode count
sections.text: Both models approach 3nR at high temperature. If an imported DOS gives the wrong plateau, first check frequency units, DOS normalization, missing branches, and the molar convention.

sections.title: Material parameters need sources
sections.text: The demonstration's θE and θD are adjustable teaching parameters. Before labeling a curve as a prediction for a real material, provide parameter sources or actual mesh data, and document fitting and approximations in the material research notebook.

exercises.title: Why do labels remain unchanged under a basis change within a degenerate subspace?
exercises.prompt: A three-dimensional degenerate space is spanned by orthonormal columns E, with restricted group operations Dsub.

steps.prompt: Under the basis change E′=EU, what is the restricted matrix?
steps.hint: Substitute into E′† D E′.
steps.explanation: E′†DE′=U†E†DEU, so this is a similarity transformation.

steps.prompt: What does Tr(U† Dsub U) equal?
choices: It can be changed arbitrarily by U
steps.hint: Use cyclic invariance of the trace and U†U=I.
steps.explanation: The trace is independent of an orthonormal basis change within the subspace.

steps.prompt: How do multiplicities from character inner products change?
steps.hint: The inner product uses only characters.
steps.explanation: Characters are unchanged, so the irreducible-component  multiplicity  is unchanged.

steps.prompt: If a single column from a degenerate space is not closed under the symmetry, what should be done?
choices: Restore the complete degenerate space before classifying
steps.hint: A group operation can rotate one column into other degenerate columns.
steps.explanation: Check the entire subspace; do not force an irreducible label onto a nonclosed single column.

exercises.title: Choose a periodic supercell for q=(1/2,0,0)
exercises.prompt: Use q=(1/2,0,0) in primitive reciprocal coordinates and a diagonal supercell.

steps.prompt: What is the mode phase factor after translating by one  primitive cell  along the first direction?
steps.hint: Evaluate exp(2πi×1/2).
steps.explanation: The phase advances by π, giving −1.

steps.prompt: What is the factor after translating by two  primitive cell  along the first direction?
steps.hint: Multiply by −1 once more.
steps.explanation: exp(2πi)=1, so periodicity is restored.

steps.prompt: Which minimal example  supercell  satisfies periodic boundary conditions?
steps.hint: Every ni qi must be an integer.
steps.explanation: Only the first direction needs doubling.

steps.prompt: Can an exported frozen structure immediately be identified as a stable phase?
choices: No; energies, forces and stability must also be checked
Yes, because the displacement is nonzero
steps.hint: Freezing a mode specifies only a geometric configuration.
steps.explanation: A mode snapshot is not a relaxed structure or a free-energy minimum.

exercises.title: Recover a rigid translation from  mass weighting  eigenvectors
exercises.prompt: Two atoms have masses 1 and 4, with mass-weighted eigenvector components 1/√5 and 2/√5 in one direction.

steps.prompt: What is the sum of squared moduli of these two components?
steps.hint: Calculate 1/5+4/5.
steps.explanation: The mass-weighted eigenvector is normalized.

steps.prompt: What is the second atom's displacement ratio after removing mass weighting?
steps.hint: Divide 2/√5 by √4.
steps.explanation: After undoing mass weighting, the second atom's component is 1/√5.

steps.prompt: How are the physical displacements of the two atoms related?
choices: The second is twice as large
steps.hint: Compare e1/√m1 with e2/√m2.
steps.explanation: They describe a rigid translation, providing an independent check of the acoustic zero mode.

steps.prompt: What goes wrong if physical displacements are drawn directly using the lengths of e?
choices: It incorrectly shows a larger displacement for the second atom
The frequency unit is corrected automatically
steps.hint: e uses  mass weighting  coordinates.
steps.explanation: Omitting inverse mass weighting changes the relative amplitudes of the actual atomic motion.

exercises.title: Work out the C4v E → Cs branching by hand
exercises.prompt: The restricted characters are (2,0); Cs characters for A′ and A″ are (1,1) and (1,−1).

steps.prompt: What is the order of subgroup Cs?
steps.hint: Only identity and the mirror remain.
steps.explanation: The inner-product denominator is 2.

steps.prompt: What is the multiplicity of A′?
steps.explanation: A′ occurs once.

steps.prompt: What is the  multiplicity  of A″?
steps.explanation: A″ also occurs once.

steps.prompt: What is the total dimension after restriction?
choices: 1, because the little group is smaller
steps.hint: Multiply  multiplicity  by  representation dimension , then sum.
steps.explanation: 1×1+1×1=2; lowering symmetry does not remove states.

exercises.title: From mirror protection to an avoided crossing
exercises.prompt: The two states have mirror eigenvalues +1 and −1, with local model H=dz σz+δσx.

steps.prompt: If mirror symmetry is preserved, what condition must constant mixing δ between the two states satisfy?
steps.hint: MσxM⁻¹=−σx。
steps.explanation: A constant σx mixing term changes sign, so mirror symmetry requires its coefficient to vanish.

steps.prompt: For δ=0, what happens to the levels at dz=0?
steps.hint: Diagonalize the zero matrix directly.
steps.explanation: Both energies are zero.

steps.prompt: For δ=0.2, what is the gap at the former crossing?
steps.hint: The energies are ±|δ|.
steps.explanation: The upper energy minus the lower is 2|δ|=0.4.

steps.prompt: After symmetry breaking, can ±1 remain exact mirror labels of every eigenstate?
choices: No; the Hamiltonian no longer preserves that mirror
Yes, because the parent phase has a mirror
Yes, because the matrix is still two-dimensional
steps.hint: Check [H,M] first.
steps.explanation: The parent-phase compatibility table remains a comparison, but the actual states are now mixed.

exercises.title: Where are the Rashba-split states and their Kramers partners?
exercises.prompt: H=εI+α(sin ky σx−sin kx σy), T²=−1, and initially Bz=0.

steps.prompt: What is the spin-dependent term at Γ?
steps.hint: sin 0=0。
steps.explanation: The two states at Γ are degenerate.

steps.prompt: Must a generic point on Γ–X have twofold degeneracy at the same k?
choices: Not necessarily; T generally maps k to −k
Yes; every k is a TRIM
steps.hint: Kramers degeneracy at the same momentum requires k and −k to be reciprocal-lattice equivalent.
steps.explanation: Rashba splitting is possible at generic k; its  time reversal  partner lies at −k.

steps.prompt: What are the eigenvalues of a spinful mirror with M²=−I?
steps.hint: Solve m²=−1.
steps.explanation: This is a double-valued mirror representation.

steps.prompt: After adding Bzσz, can T still guarantee degeneracy at Γ?
choices: No; the Zeeman term breaks T
steps.hint: Time reversal flips spin.
steps.explanation: The Γ-level separation becomes 2|Bz|.

exercises.title: High-temperature heat capacity of a two-atom primitive cell
exercises.prompt: Use a stable harmonic model at fixed primitive cell, with n=2 atoms per cell and R≈8.31446 J/(mol K).

steps.prompt: How many vibrational branches occur at each q?
steps.hint: Each atom has three displacement directions.
steps.explanation: There are 3n=6 branches.

steps.prompt: How much constant-volume heat capacity does each positive-frequency harmonic mode contribute at high temperature?
steps.hint: Kinetic and potential energy each contribute kBT/2.
steps.explanation: Each mode's internal energy approaches kBT and its heat capacity approaches kB.

steps.prompt: What is the approximate high-temperature Cv per mole of  primitive cell ?
How should the result be converted to a per-mole-of-atoms quantity?
steps.hint: Each primitive cell contains two atoms.
steps.explanation: The plateau per mole of atoms is 3R; the counting convention must be explicit.

exercises.title: Check normalization of the  phonon  mesh and DOS
exercises.prompt: A 2×2×2 mesh is reduced to three representative q points with weights 1,3,4; the primitive cell contains two atoms.

steps.prompt: What should the integer weights of representative points sum to?
steps.hint: The complete mesh has 2×2×2 points.
steps.explanation: 1+3+4=8, matching the complete mesh.

steps.prompt: What is the normalized weight of the third point?
steps.hint: Divide the number represented by the total point count.

steps.prompt: What should the integrated complete total DOS be per primitive cell?
steps.hint: The count is 3n modes, not the number of mesh points.
steps.explanation: There are 6 modes per  primitive cell .

steps.prompt: Can frequencies only along Γ–X directly replace this integral?
choices: No; a path does not sample Brillouin-zone volume
Yes; the more repeated endpoints, the better
steps.hint: Line sampling differs from volume sampling.
steps.explanation: Correct mesh weights or a complete, clearly normalized total DOS are required.

exercises.title: Distinguish Einstein and Debye models by their limits
exercises.prompt: Compare two three-dimensional teaching models with the same total mode count and characteristic temperature.

steps.prompt: What power of ν describes the low-frequency Debye DOS?
steps.hint: Count states in three-dimensional spherical shells.
steps.explanation: Three-dimensional wave-vector shells with linear dispersion give g(ν)∝ν².

steps.prompt: What power of T describes its sufficiently low-temperature heat capacity?
steps.hint: Use ν/T as the integration variable.
steps.explanation: The number of thermally accessible low-frequency modes grows as T³.

steps.prompt: Within the same low-temperature asymptotic regime, by approximately what factor does Debye heat capacity increase when temperature doubles?
steps.hint: (2T)³/T³。
steps.explanation: It should be approximately eightfold; the numerical curve provides an independent check.

steps.prompt: What sets the high-temperature plateau of both models?
steps.hint: Each mode contributes kB at high temperature.
steps.explanation: At the same n, both approach 3nR despite different low-temperature behavior.

cases.title: From Γ modes to frozen structures and heat capacity
cases.summary: Identify acoustic T1u and optical T2g of Oh, check displacements, and export the structure. Then investigate thermodynamics using your own mesh data.
cases.assumption: Built-in frequencies and modes are checkable teaching constructions; θE/θD are user parameters, not fitted parameters for Si.

cases.title: Different atomic masses and Td vibrational representations
cases.summary: Compare mass-weighted eigenvectors with physical displacements, understand the acoustic and optical T2 subspaces, and construct a frozen mode.
cases.assumption: This demonstration does not infer Raman intensity or actual  soft mode  frequencies from mode labels.

cases.title: Orbitals, mirrors, and crossings on a square lattice
cases.summary: Use a periodic two-orbital p_x/p_y model to calculate E→A′+A″ and mirror-breaking gaps, then switch to the spinful Rashba model.
cases.assumption: This is a two-dimensional model, not a particular real material or a catalogue of band connectivity for every space group.
